samples.summary: `moveStraddlingFreeze`'s "already straddles" exemption is whole-block, not per-axis, so a move that newly creates a *row*-axis straddle is allowed whenever the block already straddled the *column* boundary (and vice versa)
samples.evidence: Line 500-502: `if (!crossesFreezePane(after, frozenRows, frozenCols)) continue; ... if (crossesFreezePane(before, ...)) continue;`. `crossesFreezePane` ORs the row and column tests, so a single boolean answers both axes. Concrete case: frozenRows=2, frozenCols=2, merge anchored B3 with {rs:2, cs:3} covers B3:D4 — it crosses the column line (2<=2 && 4>2) but not the row line. A row move that remaps rows 3,4 to 2,3 (e.g. moving row 2 out to dst 5) leaves the block at rows 2-3, which now crosses the frozen row line. `before` is truthy (column crossing), so the newly created row-axis straddle is skipped and the move is accepted by both `Sheet.moveCells` and the v1 `POST move` handler. The stated invariant is "no writer creates one"; on a per-axis reading, this writer does. Impact is contained because the block was already undrawable in the other axis.

samples.summary: Cross-sheet grid resolver walks the raw Yorkie merges record with `Object.entries`, which the repo elsewhere treats as a throwing operation (`safeWorksheetRecordEntries` exists precisely for the duplicate-own-keys TypeError)
samples.evidence: `buildMergeCoverMap(Object.entries(ws.merges ?? {}) as Array<[Sref, MergeSpan]>)` — the rewritten block advertises defensiveness ("survives a key that is not a cell reference and a span that is not two positive integers") but still reaches the CRDT proxy through bare `Object.entries`. `packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-record.ts:47-61` documents that `Object.entries` on these Yorkie-backed records can throw `TypeError ... ownKeys ... duplicate`, and every backend reader of `ws.merges` (e.g. worksheet-structure.controller.ts:152, 193; worksheet-structure.ts:279) routes through `safeWorksheetRecordEntries`. A throw here escapes the grid resolver during formula evaluation instead of degrading to an unmerged read. Pre-existing in shape, but this delta rewrote exactly these lines and had the safe helper available.

samples.summary: The API freeze-straddle guard feeds unvalidated CRDT spans into `moveStraddlingFreeze`, which (unlike the new `buildMergeCoverMap`) does not apply `isCountableMergeSpan`, so a non-integer/NaN span silently bypasses the check
samples.evidence: `assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze` passes `safeWorksheetRecordEntries(ws.merges ?? {})` straight through. `moveStraddlingFreeze` (merging.ts:495-504) calls `moveMerge`/`toMergeRange` on the raw span; with `rs` absent or non-numeric, `anchor.r + span.rs - 1` yields NaN (or a string-concat result for `rs: "3"`), every `crossesFreezePane` comparison against NaN is false, and the guard returns null — the same NaN-poisoning failure mode the delta added `isCountableMergeSpan` (merging.ts:130-139) to close on the reader side. The engine path is safe because `rebuildMergeCoverMap` already dropped such spans from `this.merges`; the API path reads the CRDT map directly, so the two now disagree about which maps are walkable.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as quoted: sheet-view.tsx:1242-1244 builds the merge cover map from `Object.entries(ws.merges ?? {})` where `ws` is a Yorkie CRDT proxy obtained at line 1233 from `doc.getRoot()` (line 1222), inside the grid resolver registered at line 1220 for cross-sheet formula evaluation. The repo documents this enumeration as throwable: worksheet-record.ts:13-19 and 47-61 define `safeWorksheetRecordEntries`, which catches the duplicate-ownKeys TypeError and falls back to a JSON snapshot. Every other reader of `ws.merges` uses that helper, including the same frontend package on the same field (yorkie-store.ts:1072, and 977/1277/1291/1309), plus backend readers (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:152,193; worksheet-structure.ts:279,601,694). No guard upstream snapshots or normalizes `ws.merges` before line 1243; the `?? {}` only covers absence, not the enumeration error. The comment at 1236-1241 claims defensiveness, but that tolerance lives inside `buildMergeCoverMap` (merging.ts:167) and is only reached after the throwing enumeration. A throw therefore escapes the resolver during formula evaluation instead of degrading to an unmerged read — a missing-guard crash on a reachable path, squarely in the correctness lane. Nothing I found supports not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope.

finding.summary: Row/column reorder is refused whenever *any* merge straddles the freeze, including blocks the move never touches
finding.evidence: `moveCells` builds `movedMerges = moveMergeMap(this.merges, axis, src, count, dst)` and refuses ('merge-move-frozen') if ANY entry of the resulting map crosses the freeze pane. A block outside [src..src+count) and outside the dst shift window is left at the same indices by `remapIndex`, so if it straddled before the move it still straddles after — and the reorder is refused even though the move neither created nor worsened the straddle. Straddling blocks were freely creatable until this PR (merge first, then `setFreezePane`, which did not snap before), so real documents have them. The result is that row/column reordering silently stops working (and `POST .../move` answers 409 permanently) on such a tab, for moves completely unrelated to the merge. The same whole-map test is duplicated in `packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-structure.controller.ts:194` (`assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze`). Contrast `moveRangeTo` (sheet.ts:2919), which correctly only checks the *translated* blocks it actually moves. The check should compare post-move straddling against pre-move straddling and refuse only newly created ones.

verdict.reason: The described code does not exist in this repository. `moveCells` (sheet.ts:1574-1587) does not build a moved merge map and test every entry against the freeze pane; it calls `moveStraddlingFreeze(this.merges, axis, src, count, dst, this.frozenRows, this.frozenCols)` and refuses only on a non-null result. `moveStraddlingFreeze` (merging.ts:495-505) performs exactly the before/after comparison the finding recommends: for each block it computes the post-move range, skips it if it does not cross the freeze, and then explicitly skips it again if the *pre-move* range already crossed (`if (crossesFreezePane(before, ...)) continue;`) — so a pre-existing straddler never refuses a move. The `moveMergeMap` call at sheet.ts:1624 is the post-guard remap, not the check. The backend controller is not a duplicated whole-map test either: `assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze` (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:185-208) delegates to the same `moveStraddlingFreeze` and throws only on its non-null anchor. A regression test at packages/sheets/test/sheet/merge.test.ts:1167-1189 builds the exact scenario in the finding (freeze 2 rows, load a straddling A1:A4 block via the store, move an unrelated row) and asserts the move succeeds with zero refusals. The proposed fix is already the implemented behavior.
